# We act for Altamira Health Technologies, Inc. on its proposed acquisition of Sorell Diagnostics B.V. Today is September 15, 2025. Using only the transaction su…

## What is the value of the transaction for HSR purposes?

As a result of the acquisition Altamira will hold voting securities valued at $228.5 million: the $212.5 million Purchase Price plus the $16.0 million value of the 8% stake it already holds (aggregated under 801.13). [F1]

## Which HSR size-of-transaction thresholds apply to this deal?

Because $228.5 million is above $126.4 million but not more than $505.8 million, the size-of-person test applies. [F2] [F1]

## What are the annual net sales of Altamira and of Sorell for the HSR size-of-person test?

The size-of-person test is satisfied: Altamira's annual net sales of $3.1 billion exceed $252.9 million and Sorell's annual net sales of $337 million exceed $25.3 million. [F3]

## Is the foreign issuer exemption available for the acquisition of Sorell?

The foreign issuer exemption in 802.51 is not available because Sorell made sales in or into the United States of $138.0 million in its most recent fiscal year, above the $126.4 million limit (its $22.0 million of US assets is below the limit, but either prong defeats the exemption). [F4]

## What HSR filing fee is payable for this transaction?

An HSR filing is required and the filing fee is $105,000 (transaction value of $179.4 million or more but less than $555.5 million). [F5]

## When does the HSR waiting period expire?

If filed on October 6, 2025, the initial 30-day waiting period would expire on November 5, 2025 (a Wednesday), absent early termination or a Second Request. [F6]

## What pre-closing conduct or integration steps does the deal allow Altamira before clearance?

The plan for Altamira's commercial team to take over Sorell's US pricing decisions and sales representatives from signing is gun-jumping: it transfers operational control before the HSR waiting period expires and breaches the EUMR Article 7 standstill. It must be stopped. [F7]

## What is the parties' combined worldwide turnover under the EU Merger Regulation?

Article 1(2) is not met: combined worldwide turnover is EUR 3,120 million (2,810 + 310), below EUR 5,000 million. [F8] [F11]

## In which Member States do both parties exceed the turnover thresholds?

Article 1(3) is met: combined worldwide turnover exceeds EUR 2,500 million, and in Germany (EUR 472 million), France (EUR 331 million) and the Netherlands (EUR 138 million) combined turnover exceeds EUR 100 million with each party above EUR 25 million. [F9]

## What is Sorell's turnover in Italy?

Italy does not count toward Article 1(3)(c): although combined Italian turnover is EUR 159 million, Sorell's Italian turnover is only EUR 9 million, below EUR 25 million. [F10]

## What is Sorell's EU-wide turnover, and does either party achieve more than two-thirds of its EU turnover in one Member State?

Sorell's EU-wide turnover of EUR 164 million and Altamira's EUR 1,200 million both exceed EUR 100 million, and neither achieves more than two-thirds of its EU turnover in one Member State, so the two-thirds rule does not apply. [F11] [F9]

## Must the transaction be notified to the European Commission, and what standstill and review timetable applies?

The concentration has an EU dimension and must be notified to the European Commission; it may not be implemented before clearance (Article 7(1) standstill), and Phase I review takes 25 working days from notification. [F12]

## What are the parties' market shares in point-of-care coagulation analyzers in the EEA?

The parties' combined EEA share of point-of-care coagulation analyzers is 41% (24% + 17%), making them the largest supplier ahead of Veltris Medical (28%) — a likely Phase I focus. [F13]

## What are the parties' market shares in the Netherlands?

In the Netherlands the combined analyzer share would be 47% (Sorell 38% + Altamira 9%). [F14]
